title: 11th Sitting of first session of 2026
summary: The sitting opened at 9:00 on Wednesday 22 April 2026 with the minutes of sittings 5 to 7 accepted and the chair announcing committee membership changes and committee deadlines. Seventeen answers followed from the Minister of Islamic Affairs, mostly on the Hajj waiting list, mosque projects and Hajj/Umrah fraud. A government bill amending the law on sexual harassment was read for the first time, then MPs began the preliminary debate on Mauroof Zakir's bill to change how resort service charge is shared. That debate was still running, with no vote, when this part of the text ends; some passages are garbled, so a few gists are approximate. This part picks up mid-debate on the bill from the Kendhoo member to amend the Employment Act so that resort service charge is paid to staff in the currency it is collected in, rather than converted to rufiyaa. MDP members backed it, saying conversion pushes staff to the black market and cuts their income; PNC members criticised it as political or said it should not be forced by law, though several said it should go to committee. The Majlis then began debating a Fisheries Act amendment before a recess, and after the break voted 67-0 to accept the Employment Act bill and send it to committee. The text begins mid-speech and is partly garbled, so some figures quoted by speakers are uncertain.

items.title: Debate on the bill to amend the Employment Act (Law 2/2008) on paying resort service charge to staff in the currency collected, by the Kendhoo member Mauroof Zakir
items.outcome: debate closed after the sponsor replied; accepted 67-0 and sent to committee

items.title: Debate on the government's bill to amend the Fisheries Act (Law 14/2019), by the South Thinadhoo member Mohamed Alsan Ahmed
items.outcome: debate begun; one speaker heard before the recess, to resume later

items.title: Vote on the Employment Act amendment bill (acceptance)
Announcement of next sitting and close of sitting
items.outcome: next sitting set for Monday 27 April 2026 at 10:00 am

speakers.name: Dr. Mohamed Shaheem Ali Saeed
positions: As Minister of Islamic Affairs, said Hajj waiting lists are long worldwide, partly from COVID-era missed trips, with some priority for those aged 65 and over.
Said a Hajj and Umrah law is being drafted to define the Hajj Corporation's role and punish fraud by companies.
Said mosque works such as Kendhoo and Fehendhoo are progressing or starting, and that large mosques are being air-conditioned with solar.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked when work on the Kendhoo and Kudarikilu mosques would finish and open.
As mover, said service charge is mostly collected in dollars but paid in rufiyaa, so resort staff lose income, and the bill extends it to front-line contract staff.
Raised a point of order that his bill was tabled on 8 December 2025, so it is unrelated to the election.
Said service charge is collected for staff, not owners, and should be paid in the currency collected; converting it to rufiyaa cuts staff income.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Asked how many mosques were contracted without funding under the previous government and for details of them.
Opposed the service charge bill, saying it was drafted hastily and that the government is preparing wider Employment Act changes.
Said consultation with resort staff and industry stakeholders is needed before such amendments.
Raised a point of order that some resorts also accept rufiyaa and other currencies, and said earlier claims by MDP members were inaccurate.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked about upgrading pilgrims' tents at Mina and the roles of the minister and President on the Makkah-Madinah high-speed rail.
Backed the service charge bill, saying staff should receive service charge in the form it is collected.
Said he sought a second turn, called the bill a build-on-gains measure, and said owners profited for decades before cutting staff in COVID.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked whether Saudi upgrades, the high-speed train and hotel improvements will benefit Maldivians, as the minister's answer suggested.
Said paying service charge in rufiyaa drives staff to the black market, and the bill helps staff and the economy.
On the Fisheries Act amendment, said fishermen's main problems are low prices, loans and unmet pledges, and that new restrictions would burden them.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Opposed the bill, saying it would reduce resort staff opportunities and income, and alleged a political motive after the local council elections.
Said the bill would not be accepted by the Majlis and urged the mover to withdraw it.
Supported the bill, saying service charge must not be converted, and staff serving tourists through contractors or short contracts should be treated alike.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Asked when the list of people chosen for Hajj, who have paid, will be made public.
Complained that an answer to his August 2025 question only came in April 2026 and asked for faster replies.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Asked about the ministry's preparations and facilities for the Hajj season (text partly garbled).
Said the bill's intent looks sound but its effects need thought, and that staff lose out when dollar service charge is converted to rufiyaa.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Asked how soon work will begin to enlarge the very small mosque on Fehendhoo, given its population.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Thanked the ministry for the Vaikaradhoo Quran centre and asked when the Islamic centre and Nelaidhoo mosque works start and when the Hajj list is published.
Said the amendment is simple: service charge should go to staff as collected, and the bill was delayed since December.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the amendment could clash with other laws, such as the foreign exchange law, and that tourism needs careful handling.
Said he could not support the bill as tabled and that the government will bring a better solution.
Said the second amendment on non-permanent workers is hard to apply, criticised MDP's record, and said PNC would accept the bill for committee consultation.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Asked why the Hajj list has grown so long and what the government has done about it since taking office.

speakers.name: Abdul Rahman
positions: Asked why people given Hajj places through gifts or companies get priority, and why couples cannot be sent together.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Asked on what principle the Hajj order was changed, noting people with 2026 places were moved to 2027.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked what the minister is doing to give ill or elderly people who could not go to Hajj further chances.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Asked what further steps are planned against Umrah companies and groups that take money and cheat customers.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Praised the ministry's Quran centre work and asked how confident the minister is that Maldives' Hajj quota will grow.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: Asked what the ministry is doing now, before a law passes, about private parties collecting money for Umrah trips and failing to deliver.

speakers.name: Adam Shafeeq
positions: Asked how many mosques have been air-conditioned so far under the mosque AC programme.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Opposed the service charge bill, calling it poorly drafted, and defended the government's economic record, citing bank deposits and lending.
Urged the opposition to avoid street protests amid the global fuel price rise.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Supported the bill, saying resort staff are worried that the 10% service charge loses value when dollars are converted at a different rate.
Said a committee had earlier worked on the mover's amendment and that many staff in his area share the concern.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Said MDP did not change this law when in government, called the bill political, and argued the country should use rufiyaa and not be pushed toward dollars.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said MDP's group filed the bill after resort staff complaints, and linked the gap between the official and black-market dollar rates to the problem.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Said staff should be paid in dollars if the business earns dollars, but opposed forcing it by law, and criticised MDP's record and motives.

decisions: The minutes of sittings 5 to 7 (nos. 2026/1/5 to 2026/1/7) were accepted by the chair as no amendments were submitted.

Committee changes announced from 20 April 2026: Hamad Abdulla joins Safety Services and Ahmed Xamyr joins Finance, both replacing Ahmed Nazim, who moves to Environment and Climate Change replacing Mohamed Mamdooh.

Committee deadlines announced: Judiciary Committee reports on Penal Code, Courts Act and Evidence Act amendment bills due 15 June 2026, and the National Service Bill (Safety Services Committee) due 31 July 2026.
The government bill amending Law 16/2014 (sexual harassment and abuse) was read for the first time.
The Employment Act service charge bill had its preliminary debate under way at the end of this part; no vote was taken in this part.
The chair closed debate on the Employment Act amendment bill after the sponsor's reply.
The Majlis voted 67-0 to accept the Employment Act (Law 2/2008) amendment bill, and under rule 106 of its rules sent it to committee.
The chair explained the bill was submitted on 8 December 2025, after the Majlis had last sat on 3 December 2025, so it could not be put on the agenda earlier.
Debate on the Fisheries Act (Law 14/2019) amendment bill began and was paused for the recess.
Next sitting announced for Monday 27 April 2026 at 10:00 am.

votes.what: Accepting the Employment Act (Law 2/2008) amendment bill by Mauroof Zakir (93 members in total, 69 present, 67 voted, 34 needed)
